new_assertions.title: shortest obstruction forces a model change
new_assertions.body: Within one-Boolean-value-per-current-quotient-node semantics, no exact successor model can simultaneously preserve both shortest 5x4 routes, their current shared source/target quotient identifications, and all four current edge-delta constraints while making the phase path-independent. At least one of those load-bearing conditions must change.
new_assertions.scope: shortest 5x4 obstruction under scalar Boolean node-potential semantics

new_assertions.title: state-refinement-only repair must break a shared endpoint identification
new_assertions.body: If the two shortest 5x4 routes, their four edge deltas, and one Boolean value per refined node are retained unchanged, any repair achieved solely by state refinement must separate at least one currently shared route endpoint occurrence; retaining both current shared endpoint identifications reproduces the inconsistent constraint system.
new_assertions.scope: shortest 5x4 obstruction; conditional on state-refinement-only repair

new_assertions.title: unchanged quotient and deltas force departure from scalar node-potential semantics
new_assertions.body: If both current shared quotient endpoint identifications and all four shortest-witness edge deltas are retained, the witness cannot be made path-independent by assigning one Boolean phase value to each current quotient node; a successful correction must instead change the phase codomain/edge semantics, refine the quotient, remove an asserted route/edge, or abandon scalar path-independence.

new_assertions.title: an erased residual distinction lies directly on the obstructed quotient seam
new_assertions.body: The shortest 5x4 scalar obstruction occurs across quotient nodes that merge represented fine states with residual-membership differences; therefore an exact fine residual distinction is present at the same quotient seam where scalar path consistency fails.
new_assertions.note: Presence at the seam is exact; causal sufficiency is not asserted.

new_assertions.title: continuation obstruction does not falsify the binary-tie XOR layer
new_assertions.body: The represented 5x4 scalar continuation obstruction and the represented binary-tie XOR-zero equivalence are jointly satisfiable because they constrain distinct predicates/carriers; the continuation counterexample does not negate the exact binary-tie relation.
new_assertions.scope: packet-local scope separation between continuation and binary-tie layers
